The high-risk patient is one who is currently ventilating and oxygenating adequately but is in respiratory distress and has the potential to rapidly deteriorate.
Mechanisms of injury that warrant an ESI 2 designation include falls of 20 feet (6 meters) or more
If that is the case the patient would be an ESI level 5
Clinical presentations requiring lifesaving interventions include the following: intubated, unresponsive, pulselessness, apneic, severe respiratory distress, profound hypotension or hypoglycemia.
Reassess to determine whether the patient warrants a higher acuity level if a patient has one or more vital signs outside the normal parameters for the patient.
1-28 days of age: Assign at least ESI 2 if T > 38° C
